newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse ends up on Friday as dollar supports.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse ends up on Friday as dollar supports.

text.p: French shares ended firmer, benefitting from dollar strength, traders said. Volume was fairly thin ahead the long weekend with markets closed on Monday for the national July 14 holiday.

The market pretty much shrugged off U.S. producer prices data in the afternoon and barely reacted to the German budget announcement that the public deficit for 1997 would be three percent of GDP, they said.
The CAC-40 index closed up 12.5, or 0.43 percent,at 2,941.59. The index was up 0.24 percent on the week.
The CAC-40 July futures finished up at 2,950 versus 2,933 at Thursdays close.
The broader SBF120 index was up 7.02 at 2,008.47
Total volume was around 4.8 billion francs.

* LVMH closed up 0.06 percent at 1,571. The luxury goods group declined to comment on a Guardian newspaper report that chairman Bernard Arnault would present his proposals for drinks merger with Guinness and Grand Met.
* Eurotunnel ended down 6.21 percent at 7.55, after forging ahead at the opening and hitting a day high of 8.95 francs before running into profit-taking. Volume was a heavy 18 million shares.
* Cap Gemini continues to firm, up 2.59 percent to 376.5, after holding company CGIP raised its stake in the computer systems house to 30 percent from 20.
* Index heavyweight Elf Aquitaine was busy with 210 million francs of shares changing hands. The stock closed up 0.46 percent at 661.
